results.title: Matrix determinant lemma without invertibility
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The matrix determinant lemma, without any invertibility hypothesis: the determinant of a rank-one update of `A` is `det A` plus the adjugate pairing `v ⬝ᵥ (adjugate A *ᵥ u)`. This is the general version left as a TODO in Mathlib's `Matrix.det_add_replicateCol_mul_replicateRow`.

results.title: Matrix determinant lemma in column-times-row form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The matrix determinant lemma in the `replicateCol` / `replicateRow` form stated in Mathlib's TODO for `Matrix.det_add_replicateCol_mul_replicateRow`. The `_general` suffix avoids clashing with Mathlib's invertible version of the same name.

results.title: Invertibility criterion for a rank-one update
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A rank-one update of `A` is a unit exactly when the adjugate correction term is a unit; no invertibility hypothesis on `A` is needed.

results.title: Multiplicative matrix determinant lemma for invertible matrices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The matrix determinant lemma in multiplicative form, when `A.det` is a unit: this recovers Mathlib's `Matrix.det_add_replicateCol_mul_replicateRow` from the general version.

results.title: Farey staircase
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a real number $x$, the Farey staircase of order $n$ is $A_n(x) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=1}^{n} \lfloor kx \rfloor / k$, the average of the first $n$ lower rational approximations $\lfloor kx \rfloor / k$ of $x$. For $n = 0$ the sum is empty and $A_0(x) = 0$.

results.title: The Farey staircase of order zero vanishes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $x$, the Farey staircase $A_0$ of order $0$ satisfies $A_0(x) = 0$.

results.title: The Farey staircase of order one is the floor function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $x$, the Farey staircase $A_1$ of order $1$ satisfies $A_1(x) = \lfloor x \rfloor$.

results.title: Zoomed Farey staircase
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a real number $x$, the zoomed Farey staircase of order $n$ is $B_0(x) = 0$ for $n = 0$ and $B_n(x) = n A_n(x/n)$ for $n \ge 1$, where $A_n$ is the Farey staircase of order $n$. For $n \ge 1$ this equals $\sum_{k=1}^{n} \lfloor (k/n) x \rfloor / k$.

results.title: The zoomed Farey staircase as a sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$ and every real number $x$, the zoomed Farey staircase $B_n$ of order $n$ satisfies $B_n(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \lfloor (k/n) x \rfloor / k$.

results.title: The zoomed Farey staircase of order one is the floor function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $x$, the zoomed Farey staircase $B_1$ of order $1$ satisfies $B_1(x) = \lfloor x \rfloor$.

results.title: Limit of the Farey staircase zoomed at the origin
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $B_n$ be the zoomed Farey staircase of order $n$. For every real $x \ge 0$, $B_n(x) \to \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor x \rfloor} \log(x/k)$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Limit of the Farey staircase zoomed at a rational point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $B_n$ be the zoomed Farey staircase of order $n$, let $x \ge 0$ be real, and let $p$ and $q$ be coprime positive integers. Then $B_n(x + pn/q) - B_n(pn/q) \to \frac{1}{q} \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor qx \rfloor} \log(qx/k)$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Limit of the rescaled Farey staircase increment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A_n$ be the Farey staircase of order $n$ and $D_n = A_n - A_{n-1}$. For every real $x \ge 0$, $n^2 D_n(x/n) \to \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor x \rfloor} (1 - \log(x/k))$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Floor gaps of Farey staircases are dense above $1 - \log 2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $n \ge 1$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}$ let $f_n(x) = \lfloor nx \rfloor - n A_n(x)$, where $A_n$ is the Farey staircase of order $n$; thus $f_n(x) = \lfloor nx \rfloor - \sum_{k=1}^n \lfloor kx \rfloor / k$. Every real number $y \ge 1 - \log 2$ lies in the closure of the set $S = \{f_n(x) : n \ge 1,\ x \in \mathbb{R}\}$, that is, $S$ is dense in $[1 - \log 2, \infty)$.

results.title: Finiteness of small floor gaps of the Farey staircase
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $n \ge 1$ and a real number $x$, let $f_n(x) = \lfloor nx \rfloor - n A_n(x)$, where $A_n$ is the Farey staircase of order $n$. Then for every real number $\varepsilon > 0$, only finitely many distinct real numbers that are at most $1 - \log 2 - \varepsilon$ occur as a value $f_n(x)$ with $n \ge 1$ and $x$ real; here $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

results.title: Recursion between consecutive Farey staircases
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 2$ be a natural number and $x$ a real number, write $A_m$ for the Farey staircase of order $m$, and let $D_n(x) = A_n(x) - A_{n-1}(x)$. Then $D_n(x) = \frac{1}{n} \left( \lfloor nx \rfloor / n - A_{n-1}(x) \right)$ and $D_n(x) = \frac{1}{n-1} \left( \lfloor nx \rfloor / n - A_n(x) \right)$.

results.title: Bounds comparing the Farey staircase with $\lfloor nx \rfloor / n$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$ and every real number $x$, the Farey staircase $A_n$ of order $n$ satisfies $A_n(x) \le \lfloor nx \rfloor / n \le A_n(x) + (\log n)/n$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

results.title: Bounds on the increment of the Farey staircase
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 2$ be a natural number and $x$ a real number, and write $A_m$ for the Farey staircase of order $m$. Then $0 \le A_n(x) - A_{n-1}(x) \le \frac{\log n}{n(n-1)}$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

results.title: Harmonic blocks versus the logarithmic integral
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(a_n)$ and $(b_n)$ be sequences of natural numbers with $a_n \le b_n$ for every $n$ and $a_n \to \infty$. Then $\sum_{k=a_n}^{b_n} 1/k - \int_{a_n}^{b_n} dt/t \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Dilation derivative of a differentiable function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ have derivative $f'$ at the point $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Then the quotient $(\lambda^{-1} f(\lambda x) - f(x))/(\lambda - 1)$ tends to $x f' - f(x)$ as $\lambda \to 1$ with $\lambda \ne 1$; that is, the dilation derivative of $f$ at $x$ exists and equals $x f' - f(x)$.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $s = (s_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a sequence and let $i$, $\ell$ and $i'$ be natural numbers. The factor of $s$ of length $\ell$ starting at position $i$ occurs at position $i'$ when $s_{i'+t} = s_{i+t}$ for every natural number $t < \ell$.

results.title: Recurrent sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A sequence $s : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ is recurrent if every occurrence of a factor is followed by a later occurrence: for all $i, \ell \in \mathbb{N}$ there is $j > 0$ such that $s(i + j + t) = s(i + t)$ for every $t < \ell$.

results.title: Powers of $\gamma(0)$ modulo $p$ stabilize at a matrix unit
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $r, m \ge 0$ be natural numbers, let $T = \{-m, \dots, m\}^r \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^r$, and let $\gamma(0)$ be the $T \times T$ matrix over $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ whose $(i, j)$ entry is $1$ if $i = p j$ and $0$ otherwise. Then there is $s \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $s' \ge s$, $\gamma(0)^{s'}$ is the matrix whose $(0, 0)$ entry is $1$ and whose other entries are $0$.

results.title: Graphs without cycles of lengths $2k-1$ and $2k$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, a simple graph $G$ is free of the cycle lengths $2k-1$ and $2k$ when it contains no copy of the cycle graph $C_{2k-1}$ and no copy of the cycle graph $C_{2k}$, where a copy is an injective graph homomorphism, that is, a subgraph that need not be induced.

results.title: Extremal number for cycles of lengths $2k-1$ and $2k$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, $\mathrm{ex}(n; \{C_{2k-1}, C_{2k}\})$ is the supremum of the numbers of edges of the simple graphs on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that contain no copy of the cycle graph $C_{2k-1}$ and no copy of the cycle graph $C_{2k}$, where the supremum of the empty set is $0$. Here $2k-1$ is computed in the natural numbers, so it is $0$ when $k = 0$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: It is not the case that for every natural number $k \ge 2$ the ratio $\mathrm{ex}(n; \{C_{2k-1}, C_{2k}\}) / (n/2)^{1 + 1/k}$ tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$. part.title: Labeled directed graphs
api: Restriction of a labeled directed graph

results.title: Labeled directed graph
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A labeled directed graph with vertex set $V$, edge set $E$ and label set $L$ consists of a source map $s : E \to V$, a target map $t : E \to V$ and a label map $\ell : E \to L$; the edge $e$ goes from $s(e)$ to $t(e)$ and carries the label $\ell(e)$. Loops and parallel edges are allowed.

results.title: Extensionality for labeled directed graphs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Two labeled directed graphs $G$ and $H$ with the same vertex set, edge set and label set are equal if they have the same source map, the same target map and the same label map.

results.title: Restriction of a labeled directed graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a labeled directed graph with vertex set $V$ and label set $L$, and let $p$ be a predicate on $V$. The restriction of $G$ to $p$ is the labeled directed graph with label set $L$ whose vertices are the vertices $v$ of $G$ with $p(v)$, whose edges are the edges of $G$ whose source and target both satisfy $p$, and in which each edge has the same source, target and label as in $G$.

results.title: Source of an edge in a restriction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a labeled directed graph, $p$ a predicate on its vertices, and $e$ an edge of $G$ whose source and target satisfy $p$, viewed as an edge of the restriction of $G$ to $p$. The source of $e$ in the restriction, viewed as a vertex of $G$, is the source of $e$ in $G$.

results.title: Target of an edge in a restriction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a labeled directed graph, $p$ a predicate on its vertices, and $e$ an edge of $G$ whose source and target satisfy $p$, viewed as an edge of the restriction of $G$ to $p$. The target of $e$ in the restriction, viewed as a vertex of $G$, is the target of $e$ in $G$.

results.title: Label of an edge in a restriction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a labeled directed graph, $p$ a predicate on its vertices, and $e$ an edge of $G$ whose source and target satisfy $p$, viewed as an edge of the restriction of $G$ to $p$. The label of $e$ in the restriction is its label in $G$.

results.title: Charged comparison
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For elements $x$ and $y$ of a linearly ordered type, this computation returns the truth value of $x \le y$ and charges one unit of time.

results.title: Costed insertion into a list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $a$ be an element of a linearly ordered type. Inserting $a$ into the empty list returns $[a]$ at no cost. Inserting $a$ into a list with head $b$ and tail $l$ first charges one unit for comparing $a \le b$; if $a \le b$ it returns $a$ followed by $b$ and $l$, and otherwise it inserts $a$ into $l$, adding that cost, and returns $b$ followed by the result.

results.title: Insertion sort with comparison cost
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: On a list over a linearly ordered type, insertion sort returns the empty list at no cost when the input is empty. On a list with head $a$ and tail $l$, it sorts $l$ and then inserts $a$ into the result by costed insertion; its cost is the cost of sorting $l$ plus the cost of that insertion. Exactly one unit is charged for each order comparison.

results.title: Costed insertion returns the ordered insertion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an element $a$ and a list $l$ over a linearly ordered type, the list returned by costed insertion of $a$ into $l$ is the ordered insertion of $a$ into $l$ with respect to $\le$: $a$ is placed immediately before the first element $b$ of $l$ with $a \le b$, or at the end of $l$ if there is no such element.

results.title: Cost-annotated insertion sort returns the standard insertion sort
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $xs$ over a linearly ordered type, the list returned by insertion sort with comparison costs equals the standard insertion sort of $xs$ with respect to $\le$, which inserts the head into the sorted tail.

results.title: Agreement with CSLib's monadic insertion sort
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a list $l$ over a linearly ordered type in the lowest universe, the costed insertion sort of $l$ equals CSLib's generic monadic insertion sort run in the time-counting monad with the charged comparison: the returned lists agree and the numbers of charged comparisons agree.

results.title: Insertion sort returns a sorted list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $l$ over a linearly ordered type, the list returned by insertion sort on $l$ is nondecreasing.

results.title: Insertion sort permutes its input
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $l$ over a linearly ordered type, the list returned by insertion sort is a permutation of $l$; in particular every element occurs in it exactly as often as in $l$.

results.title: Correctness of insertion sort
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $l$ over a linearly ordered type, the list returned by insertion sort is nondecreasing and is a permutation of $l$.

results.title: Cost of a single insertion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an element $a$ and a list $l$ over a linearly ordered type, costed insertion of $a$ into $l$ charges at most $n$ comparisons, where $n$ is the length of $l$.

results.title: Comparison bound for insertion sort
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On a list of length $n$ over a linearly ordered type, insertion sort charges at most $n(n-1)/2$ comparisons.
